page: Amazon Web Services c6g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 processor, utilizing the Neoverse-N1 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with 1.0 thread per core, which eliminates simultaneous multithreading overhead. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. There is no local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most multi-threaded and compute-intensive workloads. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 48574.31 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11649.0, placing both in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth is strong for cached small-block reads at 1894.03 GB/sec, but drops to 163.55 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-core performance represents a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core scoring 958.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 20.33 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 25% tier.

Given the dedicated physical core architecture and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the c6g.8xlarge is designed for compute-bound workloads that benefit from consistent core performance without hyperthreading interference. It is suited for multi-threaded applications such as software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale database operations, where it demonstrates average benchmark throughput. However, it is less suited for single-threaded tasks or memory-bound applications due to weaker single-core metrics and lower memory-to-core density. Qualitatively, the ARM-based architecture offers a resource-efficient alternative to x86 instances for workloads optimized for multi-core scaling.
